According to the mechanical performance at room temperature in the previous section, the overall performance of the CoCrFeNi(Al0.3Ti0.2)x HEA was optimal when x = 0.75. Therefore the CoCrFeNiAl0.225Ti0.15 HEA was selected for the high-temperature tensile experiments.

Experimental alloys were prepared in an arc melting furnace, and raw materials were high-purity (>= 99.9%) Co, Cr, Fe, Ni, Ti, and Al metals. To prevent segregation of the alloy components, melting the master alloys was repeated four times to finally obtain oblate alloy ingots with a maximum diameter of about 38 mm and a thickness of about 12 mm.

process_steps.method: vacuum sealing and homogenization heat treatment

evidence.quote: To eliminate the alloys' casting stress, we placed all the alloy flakes in a quartz tube for vacuum sealing, heated to 1000 C in a box-type electric furnace for 8 h, and then water-cooled and quenched.

parameters.deformation: thickness reduced from 3 mm to 1.5 mm; reduction per pass 0.05 mm

evidence.quote: The alloys with a thickness of 3 mm were rolled to 1.5 mm using a cold-rolled strip experimental rolling mill. The reduction in a single pass was 0.05 mm.

Subsequently, the rolled samples were kept at 800 C for 2 h and then cooled and annealed in the furnace. This allowed the formation of the maximum number of effective strengthening phases in the alloy, which improved the mechanical properties.
The CoCrFeNi(Al0.3Ti0.2)x HEA retains its dual-phase structure composed of the FCC matrix phase and gamma' phase with the increase of Ti and Al contents, and other phases are not formed.
The gamma' phase has Ni3(Al, Ti) molecular formula and a face-centered cubic crystal structure of L12.
